newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech, German presidents to meet as war woes linger.
newsitem.headline: Czech, German presidents to meet as war woes linger.

text.p: The Czech and German presidents will meet in Berlin next month, according to a Prague announcement on Friday, and are likely to tackle problems still lingering 50 years after World War Two ended.

At issue is a delayed declaration aimed at settling questions arising from the Nazi occupation of what is now the Czech Republic and the expulsion of around 2.5 million ethnic Sudeten Germans in the aftermath of the war.
Czech President Vaclav Havel's office did not specifically mention the declaration but he has taken an active role in pushing negotiations on the issue forward.
German President Roman Herzog said some people had expected the declaration to be ready in September when the two leaders last met, and he asked young Czechs and Germans to be patient.
In September, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said he would like to see an agreement approved by the end of the year.
But Edmund Stoiber, premier of the southern German state of Bavaria where many Sudeten Germans and their offspring live, cast doubt this week on whether the deadline could be met.
Stoiber has taken a harder line on the declaration than the Bonn government.
Czech politicians have also disagreed among themselves on the wording of the declaration.
